newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha rallies due to crudes, active buying.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha rallies due to crudes, active buying.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices rose sharply in afternoon trade on Wednesday, pulled up by firmer crudes as well as vigorous buying by a Japanese trading house, market participants said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half June was quoted at $239.00/240.50. It was sold at $234.00, $234.50, and $234.75 to the Japanese trader in late Tuesday dealing, traders said.
Second-half May was assessed at $243.00/244.50, compared with Tuesday's $237.00/237.75.
Near-term naphtha prices jumped nearly by $28, or 13 percent, in the last two weeks.

In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, Indonesia's state-owned Pertamina, region's major fuel oil supplier, is expected to announce its initial allocation for April loading later this week, traders said.
Initial allotment for April is likely to total about 3.7 million barrels, unchanged from March, they said.
About one million barrels of the forthcoming April allocation are expected to be destined for Japan, compared with some 1.6 million barrels in February and about 1.2 million in March, they said.
